chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Mubarak, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a drop of wine or an intoxicating Nabeez that dropped into a pot containing much meat and much broth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Pour out the broth, or feed it to the Ahl Al-Zimma or the dogs; and as for the meat, wash it and eat it.' I said, 'And if blood dropped into it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The blood is consumed by the fire, if Allah wills.' I said, 'So what if wine or Nabeez dropped into dough, or blood?' He said: 'It spoils.' I said, 'Can I sell it to the Jews and Christians and clarify it to them, for they permit drinking it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'And Al-Fuqa' (a type of fermented drink), is it in the same status if a drop of that drops into something?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that I eat it if a drop of that drops into something of my food.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.الْفُقَّاعُ: Al-Fuqa' (a specific type of fermented drink)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on food contaminated by a drop of wine or blood according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of 'mixing' (ikhtilat) by distinguishing between the impurity of the liquid itself versus the substance it contaminates, ruling that while broth is discarded, solid meat requires only washing. It further highlights the pragmatic application of 'Ahl al-Kitab' (People of the Book) consuming wine, allowing its sale to them, while the Imam expresses personal dislike (karahat) for fermented drinks mixed with food, reflecting the distinction between ritual purity and practical consumption in Ja'fari fiqh.
